tour.name: Tahiti Private Circle Island Tour: Point Venus, Waterfalls, Marae, Gardens & Teahupo’o

tour.overview:
Tahiti, the largest island of French Polynesia, is formed by two volcanoes joined by a narrow isthmus, Tahiti Nui and Tahiti Iti. A coastal road of about 115 kilometres circles the larger part, past black-sand beaches, waterfalls, gardens and sacred sites. It was here that the explorers Wallis, Bougainville and Cook arrived in the 18th century, and here that the painter Paul Gauguin lived.

This private day takes you around the island with a local guide and a vehicle, with time for walks to the waterfalls and a lunch by the sea.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Tahiti
• Type: private tour with local guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Point Venus.
• The Arahoho blowhole.
• The Faarumai waterfalls.
• The Taravao plateau and Teahupo’o.
• The Vaipahi gardens.
• The Maraa grotto and Marae Arahurahu.

WHY THIS WORKS
Tahiti is often treated as a stopover; your guide reveals its culture and landscapes, and the car covers the whole island.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples and anyone with a day in Tahiti.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the wild interior, choose our Papenoo valley 4x4 tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The east coast is wetter and greener; bring a light rain jacket.

days.name: Point Venus, the east coast, Teahupo'o and the west coast
days.description:
What to expect: the whole of Tahiti Nui and a glimpse of Tahiti Iti, with a local guide, private vehicle and lunch.

Your guide collects you at about 8:30 and drives east to Point Venus, a black-sand beach with a lighthouse of 1867, where Captain Cook observed the transit of Venus in 1769 and the Bounty anchored in 1788. Along the wild east coast, you see the Arahoho blowhole, where waves force spray through the lava rock, and walk through the rainforest to the Faarumai waterfalls, the tallest of which, Vaimahuta, drops into a pool among giant ferns.

At the Taravao plateau, on the isthmus, you look over Tahiti Iti, and continue to the end of the road near Teahupo'o, where one of the world's heaviest waves breaks on the reef; it hosted the surfing events of the 2024 Olympic Games. Lunch is by the sea.

On the west coast, you walk in the Vaipahi water gardens, among tropical plants and waterfalls, see the Maraa grotto with its fern-hung cave lakes, and visit the Marae Arahurahu, a restored temple of stone platforms and tiki. You return to your hotel at about 15:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:00 – Point Venus.
09:45 – Arahoho blowhole.
10:15 – Faarumai waterfalls.
11:30 – Taravao plateau.
12:00 – Teahupo’o and lunch.
13:45 – Vaipahi gardens.
14:30 – Maraa grotto.
15:00 – Marae Arahurahu.
15:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A visit to the Museum of Tahiti and the Islands can be added.
• A boat to see Teahupo’o close up can be arranged.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local guide, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we swim at the waterfalls?
faq.answer: Sometimes, depending on conditions; there is also time for a swim at a beach.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The walk to the waterfalls is short and flat.

faq.question: Can we see the Teahupo’o wave up close?
Can we add a museum?
faq.answer: Yes, the Museum of Tahiti and the Islands, on the west coast.

faq.question: Does it work with a cruise stop?
faq.answer: Yes. We adapt the timing to your ship.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, comfortable shoes, a rain jacket and sun cream.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. May to October is drier.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in French Polynesia and is never expected, but a small gesture for excellent service is always appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
